title: Isolating plasma extracellular vesicles from mouse blood using size-exclusion chromatography, density gradient, and ultracentrifugation
protocol: Anesthetize the mouse with a cocktail of ketamine 100 mg/kg and xylazine 10 mg/kg, injected intraperitoneally.
Wait for at least 10 minutes to allow sedation.
Moisten hairs with ethanol 70%.
Incise the skin to make a buttonhole facing the upper part of the thoracic cage at the level of the first ribs.
Homogenize total blood in EDTA 0.5 M microtubes at 16°C–25°C for less than 2 h.
Centrifuge the homogenized blood at 1,000 g for 15 min at 4°C.
Separate the supernatant plasma as a transparent yellow upper phase.
Prepare 1.5 mL microtubes with 30 μL EDTA 0.5 M (5% of the mean expected blood collection volume).
Flush a 1 mL syringe with 25G or 26G needle with EDTA just before plasma collection.
Localize the puncture area between the first and second ribs on the left side toward the axis.
Apply gentle suction as the syringe penetrates the muscle layer to generate a vacuum effect.
Slowly suck up 500 μL to 1 mL of blood from the heart.
Transfer quickly the collected blood into the EDTA tube.
Euthanize the mouse immediately after blood collection according to approved procedures.
Centrifuge EDTA tubes at 1,000 g for 15 min at 4°C.
Pipette carefully the supernatant and transfer it into a new collection tube.
Snap-freeze the supernatant in liquid nitrogen.
Store the frozen plasma at -80°C for further isolation or analysis.
Thaw at least 200 μl of plasma on ice for EV separation.
Prepare mouse plasma samples by differential ultracentrifugation (UC).
Combine size exclusion chromatography (SEC) with UC for EV enrichment.
Use SEC in conjunction with density gradient (DG) and UC for EV preparation.
Dilute 200 μL of freshly thawed plasma in ice-cold particle-free PBS to a final volume of 2 mL.
Centrifuge diluted plasma at 2,000 g for 10 min at 4°C to pellet large unwanted particles.
Pipette the supernatant and transfer into a new microtube.
Centrifuge the transferred supernatant at 10,000 g for 30 min at 4°C to pellet large EVs.
Pipet the supernatant and transfer into a 2 mL open-top polypropylene tube.
Centrifuge at 100,000 g for 2 hours at 4°C (maximum acceleration: 0; maximum deceleration: 0).
Discard the supernatant carefully.
Resuspend the pellet in 1 mL of ice-cold particle-free PBS.
Fill the tube up to 2 mL with particle-free PBS.
Perform additional centrifugation at 100,000 g for 2 hours at 4°C (maximum acceleration: 0; maximum deceleration: 0).
Discard the supernatant carefully by pipetting it out or by slow aspiration from the opposite side of the tube.
Resuspend the pellet in a low volume of ice-cold particle-free PBS (30–100 μL).
Centrifuge at least 200 μl and up to 600 μl of freshly thawed plasma at 10,000 g for 30 min at 4°C to pellet large particles.
Equilibrate a size exclusion chromatography column at 16°C–25°C with particle-free PBS following the manufacturer’s instructions.
Collect 500 μL of plasma supernatant for transfer onto the SEC column.
Transfer sample onto the SEC column once the plasma enters the column.
Elute the column by adding ice-cold particle-free PBS on top when the sample enters the column.
Discard the void volume (2.9 mL).
Collect the first two 500 μL EV-enriched SEC fractions (F1 and F2).
Pool F1 and F2 to obtain a total of 1 mL.
Dilute pooled EV-enriched SEC fractions to 11 mL with cold particle-free PBS in a thinwall polypropylene tube.
Pellet EVs by ultracentrifugation at 100,000 g for 2 hours at 4°C.
Carefully discard the supernatant by pipetting it out or slow aspiration from the opposite side of the tube.
Resuspend the final pellet in 30–100 μL of cold particle-free PBS for further storage and analysis.
Alternatively, lyse the pellet in 30 μL of boiling 2× denaturation SDS sample buffer for immunoblotting.
Concentrate EV-enriched fractions by ultrafiltration using 2 mL Amicon concentrators with regenerated cellulose and 10 kDa MWCO.
Prepare iodixanol working solution by mixing five volumes of iodixanol (OptiPrep, 60% w/v) stock solution with one volume of previously prepared working buffer.
Keep iodixanol working solution on ice and protected from light.
Prepare 5%, 10%, 20%, and 40% iodixanol solutions using homogenization buffer and iodixanol working solution.
Keep iodixanol solutions on ice while building the gradient.
Dispose gently 3 ml of 40% iodixanol solution in a new 13.2 ml thinwall polypropylene tube.
Gently tilt the tube horizontally and add dropwise 2.5 mL of 20% iodixanol solution.
Add dropwise 2.5 mL of 10% iodixanol solution.
Add dropwise 1.5 mL of 5% iodixanol solution.
Carefully add dropwise 1 ml of pooled EV-rich SEC fractions generated at step 7a.
Centrifuge density gradients at 100,000 g for 18 hours at 4°C.
Collect 1 mL density gradient fractions from the top using a P1000 pipette in new 1.5 mL microtubes.
Pipette fractions from the center of the meniscus with a smooth and precise action, maintaining the tip 1-2 mm below the liquid surface to avoid mixing gradient fractions.
Pool EV-enriched density gradient fractions.
Dilute them in a new 13.2 mL thinwall polypropylene tube to 11 mL with cold particle-free PBS.
Pellet EVs by ultracentrifugation at 100,000 g for 2 hours at 4°C.
Carefully discard the supernatant by pipetting it out or by slow aspiration from the side of the tube.
Resuspend the final pellet in 30–100 μL of cold particle-free PBS.
Alternatively, lyse the pellet in boiling 2× denaturation SDS sample buffer for immunoblotting.
